payload.name: Preserve All Explicitly Stated Attributes
payload.description: When a user explicitly lists multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes for liking, admiring, or valuing someone or something during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly enumerates multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes (e.g., 'brave, selfless, down-to-earth attitude'), preserve every listed item in the candidate memory; do not paraphrase away or drop any of them.
Record the attributes closely to the speaker's wording and keep them together in one memory when they describe the same target and relationship.
During CRUD, if a matching memory already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it to add any explicitly stated attributes that are missing, then stop; do not infer or add unmentioned attributes.

solves: When extracting memories from statements where a user explicitly lists multiple qualities, reasons, or attributes (for example, why they admire a person or character), the extraction step sometimes paraphrases the list into a summary and drops some listed items. This causes later questions about the omitted attributes to fail. The skill ensures every explicitly stated attribute is preserved in the memory so the full set of stated reasons remains retrievable.
